title: They made fluent children stutter — then buried the proof for 62 years
description:
In 1939, University of Iowa researcher Wendell Johnson sent a graduate student to an orphanage in Davenport, Iowa, to test whether stuttering was learned or innate. Twenty-two children were divided into groups: fluent kids were told their speech was failing and criticized relentlessly, while actual stutterers were told they sounded fine.

The experiment worked. Perfectly normal children began stammering, covering their mouths, and going silent. The graduate student, Mary Tudor, was so ashamed that she sealed the results and the paper was never published.

The story stayed buried for 62 years until a journalist uncovered the files in 2001. Iowa formally apologized, six survivors sued, and in 2007 the state paid a $925,000 settlement. But no one has ever tracked down all 22 children — or knows how many spent their entire lives stuttering without ever being told why.
